subject: Mutual Action Plan: POC environment credentialing, IP allowlist & VPC peering
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Brooks <amanda.brooks@medlytics.io>, Javier Sanchez <j.sanchez@medlytics.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Action Plan: POC environment credentialing, IP allowlist & VPC peering

Hi Amanda / Javier —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our MAP we want to lock down the POC infra tasks so your engineering team can start the evaluation next week. Below is a concise checklist and proposed timing; please confirm or flag any constraints.

POC environment checklist (what Redwood will help with / what we need from MedLytics):
- Org & project setup: Redwood service account + RBAC scoping (we’ll share SVC account email). Target: provisioned by 2026-05-08.
- API keys: one short-lived eval key (limited to 100k tokens) + long-lived test key for CI. We will hand off keys and rotation notes.
- IP allowlist: add Redwood egress CIDRs (listed in attached network template) to your firewall rules. We need at least one /24 for initial tests.
- VPC peering: exchange VPC IDs & pre-shared ASN; Redwood asks for peering maintenance window (2 hours). Proposed peering date: 2026-05-12.
- Validation: smoke test (token-gen + embedding run) and perf sweep (latency samples).

Action items for MedLytics (please confirm):
1) Confirm who will own the peering ticket and the maintenance window (contact + preferred date).
2) Provide the destination VPC ID and CIDR range you want us to peer to.
3) Add secops@medlytics.io to the allowlist ticket so your infra team can triage.

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_Draft_v2.pdf (draft MAP with timeline), redwood-network-template.yaml (CIDRs and template).

If that looks good I’ll upload the finalized MAP to the HubSpot deal and share the DocuSign for the standard POC addendum (non-binding usage commit).

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the peering runbook with your ops once you confirm the window.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Javier Sanchez <j.sanchez@medlytics.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Amanda Brooks <amanda.brooks@medlytics.io>, DevOps Team <secops@medlytics.io>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2026 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: POC environment credentialing, IP allowlist & VPC peering

Tessa —

Appreciate the clear checklist. Quick clarifications from our side:
- Peering ownership: MedLytics will open the ticket and we’ll coordinate with your network contact. I’m proposing May 12 (afternoon PT) for the window.
- CIDR question: can Redwood accept 10.40.0.0/16 as the destination range? Our infra team prefers a /16 to avoid conflicts across environments; we can restrict routing to a /24 afterwards if needed.
- API keys: we prefer you to create a scoped service account and share only the initial key via the secure HubSpot field. Can you confirm rotation guidance and whether keys can be scoped to the evaluation project only?

Also attaching a short internal note to our secops team to prep firewall rules. If you can confirm the exact outbound IPs (or CIDR min) we’ll queue change control.

Thanks — Javier
Lead DevOps Engineer
MedLytics

Javier —

Thanks for the quick reply. Short answers below and next steps:
- CIDR: 10.40.0.0/16 is fine for initial peering; we will configure route filters to limit announced prefixes to the /24 you want visible to other environments after the handoff.
- Keys & scoping: we’ll create a scoped service account tied to the MedLytics evaluation org. The initial key I’m sharing below is temporary (rotate on first use) — I’ll upload the permanent secret to the HubSpot secure field and send the link when live. Rotation guidance: rotate every 30 days for evals; we’ll provide a script in the provisioning doc.

Temporary eval key (scoped to project: medlytics-eval): rkey_eval_temp_01:eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1...
(NOTE: This key expires 2026-06-05; do not use for production.)

I’ve attached redwood-network-template.yaml with our suggested egress CIDRs and a VPC peering checklist. Proposed timeline:
- 2026-05-08: Redwood creates service account + uploads permanent key to HubSpot secure note.
- 2026-05-10: MedLytics verifies firewall pre-reqs (secops confirms ACLs).
- 2026-05-12 (15:00–17:00 PT): VPC peering window and validation.
- 2026-05-13: Smoke test + perf samples; MAP status update to stakeholders.

If that schedule works I’ll file the peering request with your ticket ID and loop in our network engineer for the runbook.

Best,
Tessa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-network-template.yaml, provisioning-keys-readme.txt

Tessa / Javier —

Thanks for the updates. From a commercial enablement side we’ll approve a 10% evaluation credit against the POC usage for MedLytics (applies to the trial month only). I’ll attach the billing note to the HubSpot deal and confirm PO steps after the smoke test completes.

Tessa — please proceed with the permanent key upload on 2026-05-08 and confirm you’ve filed the peering ticket into MedLytics’ system (include ticket ID in the HubSpot activity). Javier — if you hear any change requests from secops, loop me in so we can adjust the contract addendum quickly.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
